questions.q: My __ brother's wife is Sara - she is my aunt.
questions.explanation: We need the possessive form of 'dad'. The possessive is formed by adding apostrophe + s: **dad's**.

questions.q: __ Chelsea play Liverpool this Saturday. Do you want to come?
questions.explanation: **'Going to'** is used for a planned future event. 'I'm going to see' correctly expresses a pre-arranged plan.

questions.q: My shoes are wet, __ I'll leave them in the sun to dry.
questions.explanation: **'So'** introduces a result or consequence. The wet shoes are the cause; leaving them in the sun is the result.

questions.q: When I feel __, my face turns red.
questions.explanation: After 'feel', we use an adjective describing the subject's emotional state. **'Embarrassed'** is the correct past-participial adjective here.

questions.q: My father said I __ as late as I want.
questions.explanation: Modal verbs like **'may'** must be followed by the bare infinitive. 'May stay' is correct.

questions.q: How long does it take __ from Paris to Madrid by train?
questions.explanation: The structure **'it takes + time + to-infinitive'** is standard. 'To get' is correct.

questions.q: You need flour, eggs and sugar __ this cake.
questions.explanation: **'To make'** (infinitive of purpose) expresses why you need the ingredients.

questions.q: I __ the newspaper when the doorbell rang.
questions.explanation: **Past continuous** ('was reading') describes an action in progress in the past that was interrupted by another event (the doorbell ringing).

questions.q: I had __ very scary dream last night.
questions.explanation: We use the indefinite article **'a'** before a singular countable noun mentioned for the first time. 'Very' starts with a consonant sound, so 'a' (not 'an') is correct.

questions.q: We saw him, his wife and __ children at their home in Bristol.
questions.explanation: **'Their'** is the possessive determiner used before a noun to show belonging. 'Them' is an object pronoun and cannot precede a noun.

questions.q: He's hurt a finger on his left hand, so he can't __ the guitar.
questions.explanation: After modal verbs like **'can't'**, we always use the bare infinitive. 'Play' is correct.

questions.q: The __ school is an excellent school; they are really learning fast.
questions.explanation: **'Boys''** is the plural possessive. The school belongs to multiple boys, so the apostrophe follows the plural 's'.

questions.q: We __ anything special last weekend.
questions.explanation: **'Didn't do'** is the correct past simple negative. 'Didn't' alone needs the main verb 'do' to complete the sentence.

questions.q: I'm going to the bar to order a beer from __ barman.
questions.explanation: **'The'** is used with a specific, identifiable noun — the speaker is referring to a particular barman at that bar.

questions.q: My bicycle wheel is __ bent after my crash.
questions.explanation: **'A little'** is used as an adverb modifying the adjective 'bent', meaning slightly. 'Little' without the article has a negative connotation and does not work as a modifier here.

questions.q: We have a new picture __ the wall.
questions.explanation: **'On'** is the correct preposition for surfaces. Pictures are hung 'on' a wall.

questions.q: The first questions are simple and __ they get more complicated.
questions.explanation: **'Then'** indicates sequence — first they are simple, and after that they become more complicated.

questions.q: I work __ a bank.
questions.explanation: **'In'** is the correct preposition for working inside an institution or building: 'work in a bank/hospital/school'.

questions.q: The schoolboys all __ wear a soft grey cap on their heads.
questions.explanation: **'Have to'** expresses obligation. It follows the subject directly and takes the base form of the main verb.

questions.q: The washing machine we __ on Tuesday doesn't work.
questions.explanation: **'Bought'** is the past simple of 'buy', correct here since the purchase happened on a specific day in the past.

questions.q: I __ sing very well, so I'm going to have lessons.
questions.explanation: **'Can't'** expresses inability. The speaker is unable to sing well, which is why they are planning to take lessons.

questions.q: "I'll help you." "Thanks. __ very kind of you."
questions.explanation: **'That's'** (= That is) is used to comment on something just said or done. 'That's very kind of you' is a natural fixed expression in English.

questions.q: I fell off my bike and __ my leg.
questions.explanation: **'Broke'** is the past simple of 'break', used for a completed action at a specific past moment.

questions.q: She still feels bad, __ she's going to see the doctor today.
questions.explanation: **'So'** introduces a result or consequence. Feeling bad is the cause; seeing the doctor is the result.

questions.q: There are several reasons __ I can't help you now.
questions.explanation: **'Why'** is the correct relative adverb used after 'reasons': 'reasons why I can't help'.

questions.q: What sports __ at the leisure center?
questions.explanation: In direct questions, the auxiliary comes before the subject. **'Can we do'** follows the correct question word order: auxiliary (can) + subject (we) + main verb (do).

questions.q: __ the window, please?
questions.explanation: **'Can I open'** is correct. Modal verbs are followed by the bare infinitive, not 'to + infinitive' or the gerund.

questions.q: Please can you pass me __ cup?
questions.explanation: **'That'** is used for a singular noun distant from the speaker. Since the speaker is asking someone else to pass it, the cup is away from the speaker.

questions.q: My Uncle Frank is my __ brother.
questions.explanation: **'Dad's'** is the possessive form indicating that Uncle Frank is the brother who belongs to / is on the side of the speaker's dad.

questions.q: How many children __ she __?
questions.explanation: **'Did … have'** is the correct past simple question structure: auxiliary 'did' + subject + bare infinitive 'have'.
